newsitem.title: INDIA: India shares to consolidate, political fog clears.
newsitem.headline: India shares to consolidate, political fog clears.

text.p: Indian stocks are expected to make selective gains this week on political stability and rising liquidity, analysts said.
"The political uncertainty is over and the budget is expected to be passed," said Amit Nalinkant Dalal, a member-broker of the Bombay Stock Exchange (BSE).
"There is no reason for the market to fall."
Analysts say the pro-business 1997/98 (April/March) federal budget, held up due to a political crisis, is likely to be passed by parliament without major amendments.
Prime Minister Inder Kumar Gujral was sworn in last week to head a new government of the United Front coalition, which replaced its leader under a deal with the supporting Congress party.
The Congress triggered a crisis last month when it withdrew its support for the government, prompting a confidence vote that former prime minister H.D. Deve Gowda lost.

The focus will be on whether former finance minister P. Chidambaram's Tamil Maanila Congress (TMC) decides to rejoin the government after its leader G.K. Moopanar was passed over in the race for the new prime minister, brokers said.
"If TMC rejoins, that will give a boost to the market," said Anand Rathi, a director and BSE broker. "It would reduce the uncertainty and political bickering."
The TMC's executive committee was due to meet on Sunday to discuss whether to rejoin the government.
The widely tracked BSE's benchmark 30-share index surged 129.05 points, or 3.5 percent, to end at 3,825.57 on Friday.
Shares of state-run firms, which have been among the market out-performers in recent weeks, are likely to add to their gains on continued buying support, analysts said.
"They have become competitive. Focus will be on BHEL, MTNL (utilities) HPCL and ONGC (refineries)," Tushar Sarda, president and chief executive at Daewoo Securities, told Reuters.
Sarda said he remained bullish on the markets' outlook. "I expect the markets to be good. There's very high liquidity."
But worries remained about the poor 1996/97 earnings announcements expected from top Indian firms during the ongoing reporting season from April to June, some analysts said.

"Much of this is expected, but some investors will always be optimists, and it is unlikely that all the bad news has been factored in already -- especially as the market has focused more on the positives of the budget and the political crisis resolution," Rupa Bose, strategist at Paribas Capital Markets in Singapore said in a note to investors.
Grasim Industries, Indo-Gulf Fertilisers and Indian Rayon -- members of the Aditya Birla group -- are due to announce results next week.
